name: Parent alerts and quiet hours for the future kid agent
description: ChatGPT's parental controls set the market baseline: quiet hours, feature switches, and a notice to parents when a teen shows signs of acute distress. When Happy's kid agent ships it should have the two pieces the catalog lacks: per-kid chat hours, and an immediate alert to both parents on a safety flag instead of waiting for the nightly digest.
example: Trigger: at 21:40 the 8-year-old texts the kid agent. It answers with a fixed 'time for bed, ask me tomorrow' line. Separately, a message classified as distress sends both parents: 'Safety flag in the 10-year-old's chat at 16:12, please check in.'
how: Inside the in-house kid-safety plugin already planned for F072: `before_dispatch` claims messages outside the allowed hours and returns a fixed reply with no model call; the same hook runs the local classifier on inbound text and, on a distress or safety label, sends a pre-written supportive reply and calls the family delivery primitive (G009) to both parents with a category and time, not the transcript. `message_sending` applies the outbound check. Hours per kid come from family.json5.
depends_on: each kid having an own Apple child account and handle
caveats: A local classifier's accuracy on how 8 and 10-year-olds actually write is unproven. False alarms will annoy; misses matter more.
OpenAI puts trained human reviewers between the flag and the parent notice; a home system has none.
This is a heads-up to parents, not a crisis service, and the parents should be told so.
Not buildable before the kid agent itself, which waits for a local model.
The quiet-hours half needs no model at all (a `before_dispatch` claim with a fixed reply) and can ship the day the kid agent does; only the safety flag needs the local classifier.
ChatGPT's controls cover teen accounts; there is no market baseline for under-13 chat alerts to copy.
safety: Alerts go only to the two parents through pinned recipients and carry a category, not the child's words, to keep sensitive content out of message history. No cloud call touches kid content. If the classifier is down, the kid agent falls back to a fixed 'ask a grown-up' reply.
unverified: Whether ChatGPT's controls changed after the September 2025 launch report; OpenAI's own page returned 403 in this run.
How the plugin sends a proactive message to the parents from inside a hook; G009 covers the agent `message` tool and host jobs, and no plugin-side send path was found in the hook docs read.

name: Two-parent calendar conflict watch
description: Ohai sells avoiding conflicts across family members' calendars. Happy's version: when a new overlap appears in the next 14 days (both parents busy at a kid's pickup, two events needing the same driver), both parents get one line naming the clash, with an optional who-covers question.
example: Trigger: Tony accepts a Thursday 16:00 meeting; Jordan already has the dentist then and the 10-year-old has practice. Both get: 'Thursday 16:00: both of you are busy and practice pickup has no driver.'
how: A zero-model command job (`--command-argv`) every few hours runs a host script under the happy user: `gog calendar conflicts` (or `freebusy`) across the shared family calendar and the two parents' calendars, compares against a seen-id state file, and prints `NO_REPLY` when nothing is new. To keep each parent's data separate, the script uses one read-only credential that sees the family calendar in full and each parent's own calendar as free/busy only (Google's 'See only free/busy (hide details)' share), so the message names the family-calendar event and says only 'busy' for personal ones. The docs show a single `--to` target per job, so plan one job per parent or the parents' group chat once F006 exists; the follow-up question reuses the G010 relay.
depends_on: F009 read-only calendar on the Google path (decision 4)
each parent shares their own calendar with the reading account as free/busy only
caveats: Only applies if the calendar decision lands on Google; the iCloud path would need a different overlap script.
An overlap is not always a problem (both parents at the same recital). Without a rule such as 'kid event with no driver tag' it will cry wolf.
Happy reports; it does not move or decline anything.
Phone calendars do not warn about cross-person overlaps, so this is a gap the phone does not fill.
Whether phone calendars already warn about cross-person overlaps was not checked; if they do not, this is a gap the phone leaves open.
safety: No model call, so text in event titles cannot steer anything. The calendar grant is read-only. Personal calendars are read as free/busy only, so one parent's private event titles are not shown to the other; only shared family-calendar titles appear, the same exposure as the evening brief. The message goes only to the two parents.
unverified: Flags and JSON output of `gog calendar conflicts`: gog is not installed, only its command list page was read.
Ohai's exact behaviour beyond the marketing phrase.
Whether `gog calendar conflicts` works on calendars shared as free/busy only.

name: Sports schedule feeds with change alerts
description: TeamSnap, SportsEngine and GameChanger all give parents a calendar subscription link. Subscribing it in the family calendar gets practices and games into Happy's briefs; a small host script that polls the same link adds what the calendar subscription cannot: a text when a game moves or is cancelled. This gives G012 its real data sources and a documented reason for the script (subscribed calendars can lag by up to a day).
example: Trigger: the Saturday game's start time changes in the feed. Text: 'Soccer Saturday moved from 9:00 to 10:30, same field.'
how: Step 1 (no code): copy the link from TeamSnap (Schedule > Settings > 'Sync Calendar / Export'), SportsEngine ('Sync Schedule' > 'Other Calendar') or GameChanger's schedule sync, add it to the family calendar, and let F009 read it. Step 2: an operator-created command job (no model) every hour in season, `--command-argv '["node","scripts/ics-watch.mjs","<feed name>"]' --announce --to <parent>`, fetches the link from a file only the happy user can read, keeps a UID-to-start/location/status map in a state file, and prints one line per changed event inside the next seven days or `NO_REPLY`. The link never enters an agent's context.
caveats: TeamSnap says Google can take up to 24 hours to populate or refresh a subscribed calendar; a rainout the same morning will not reach a calendar-only path in time.
The team app's own push notification is still the fastest signal for same-day changes; the script is a backstop that also reaches the parent who does not have the app.
The subscription link is a bearer secret: anyone with it can read the schedule. Keep it out of family.json5 if that file is committed.
GameChanger lets followers sync only the game schedule according to a search summary; its help article refused this run's fetch, so only the marketing page was read.
The installed OpenClaw docs and skills contain no calendar-feed parser (a search for .ics, iCalendar and webcal found nothing), so this is a script the operator owns.
Run one job per parent with its own state file, or one job delivering to the parents' group chat once F006 exists; with a shared state file the second parent's job finds no change and stays silent.
safety: No model runs in the job; the feed is parsed by code. Event titles and locations are typed by coaches and team managers, so they are untrusted text, and the installed source mirrors a delivered announce line into the session transcript of the agent that owns the job. The script therefore prints a fixed template built from dates and times, with the title and location stripped to plain letters, digits and spaces and capped in length, and no links. Schedules contain where the kids will be and when, so the feed stays on the host and is delivered only to pinned parent handles. No RSVP or availability is ever set on the family's behalf.
unverified: GameChanger's exact rules on who can sync practices versus games.
How quickly each service's .ics link itself reflects a change (only the downstream calendar lag is documented).
Rate limits or terms for polling the subscription links hourly.

Ending health answers with 'confirm with your pediatrician' is a house rule, not a sourced requirement.

sources.title: Web search: tool parameters
sources.supports: The search tool returns at most ten results per call, so a count of eight is valid.

sources.title: Web fetch: limits and safety
sources.supports: The only hostname control in config is a denylist, so 'official sites only' cannot be set by a config key.

sources.title: Plugin hooks: tool call policy
sources.supports: A plugin hook sees each tool call's parameters and can block it, which is how an allowlist mode would be built.

sources.title: CDC: Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule by Age
sources.supports: A government health page was readable by a plain fetch and shows its own published and updated dates, the kind of dated primary source the rubric asks for.

sources.title: arXiv 2304.09848: Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines
sources.supports: Generated answers with citations are often not supported by them, so 'unclear' has to remain an accepted verdict.

name: Product and program research with live prices and links
description: 'Best kids bike helmet under $60' or 'summer camps for a 9-year-old' returns three to five options with price, dates and links; the parent does the buying.
how: Research composes `web_search`, `web_fetch` and, for JavaScript pages, the F020 browser; prices only from tool results with `fetchedAt`; no payment or booking tool is granted.
corrections: The 9 Oct notes resolved brochure PDFs by running research unsandboxed; the installed docs forbid a sandboxed caller from spawning an unsandboxed target, so remote PDFs need another path (the parent forwards the file, or the answer says it could not read it).
unverified: How often shop pages block a plain fetch was not measured; one large retailer's help page returned HTTP 503 to this run's fetch tool, which is an observation, not a citable source.
Whether web_fetch returns usable text for a PDF address is not stated in the installed docs.
The long-table email leg depends on the mailout server (F049), which is not built.

sources.title: Web fetch: limits and safety
sources.supports: The docs themselves say plain fetching fails on some sites and a browser is needed.

sources.title: PDF tool
sources.anchor: rejected when the tool runs sandboxed
sources.supports: A sandboxed agent cannot open a PDF by web address with the pdf tool, which affects camp brochures.

sources.title: Sub-agents: allowlist
sources.supports: Research cannot be run unsandboxed to get round that, because its sandboxed caller could then not spawn it.

sources.title: Cloudflare docs: Bot Fight Mode
sources.supports: Retail and ticketing sites commonly sit behind bot challenges, so live prices will often come back as 'could not verify'.

sources.title: arXiv 2304.09848: Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines
sources.supports: Unsupported claims are common in generated answers, which is why prices must come only from tool results.

name: Find a place and route errands: open-now dinner, urgent care, pharmacy, Saturday loop
description: 'Dinner tonight, open now, kids menu, nearby' or 'nearest late pharmacy' returns three picks with rating, hours, phone and a Maps link; no reservations.
how: Research calls the F021 Places MCP (`goplaces search --open-now --min-rating --lat --lng --radius-m`, `details --reviews`) and `web_fetch` for menus; real drive time needs the Routes API.
corrections: The 9 Oct note said Places lookups give no drive time so 'under 20 minutes' must be a radius; upstream goplaces now has `directions` (Routes API), so drive time is possible if that version is installed and the Routes API is enabled.
unverified: 'Kids menu' is not a filter found in the opened Places page; it would come from reading the menu page, which may be an image or PDF.
Ordering errand stops depends on the Reminders bridge (F030), not built.
Phone maps apps already answer these questions with live traffic; no source measures whether a text-based answer is used more.

sources.title: Bundled goplaces skill
sources.supports: The open-now and minimum-rating filters named in the feature are documented flags.

sources.title: Places API (New): Text Search
sources.supports: The underlying Google API supports the same filters and returns hours, phone and a Maps link.

sources.title: Routes API: get a route
sources.supports: Google's Routes API returns a traffic-aware driving duration, the piece needed for 'under 20 minutes'.

sources.title: steipete/goplaces README
sources.supports: The current upstream CLI has a directions command that returns distance and duration.
